name: LKIF Core 1.1
description: LKIF Core 1.1, the core legal ontology of the Legal Knowledge Interchange Format, developed by the University of Amsterdam, the University of Bologna and Fraunhofer FOKUS in the European ESTRELLA project (IST-2004-027665) and maintained by Rinke Hoekstra (https://github.com/RinkeHoekstra/lkif-core) under CC BY 4.0. It is a library of OWL modules for the concepts legal knowledge is built on: norms as qualifications of what is allowed, disallowed or obliged; legal sources such as statutes, regulations, contracts and precedents; rights and powers after Hohfeld and Sartor; legal persons, public bodies and public acts; legal and social roles; and the commonsense layers beneath them, from propositions, beliefs and communicated attitudes to actions, agents, processes, places, time and parthood. Generated from the Turtle files of the twelve modules LKIF Core imports: each class is a node, each object property a relationship from its domain to its range (one direction per inverse pair), each class restriction a relationship or a count, and each superclass an implied label.

AbstractEntity.description: An abstract concept is a concept which does not (necessarily) have a referent in either the physical or the mental world. Abstract entities are (proto)mathematical, formal entities, entities which have a purely formal, logical or mathematical meaning. As all concepts are abstractions, one may argue that a separate abstract world is difficult to see. In common-sense, a circle has more properties and is less abstract than in mathematics. Even mathematicians marvel about the fact their pure abstractions enable us to predict very concrete things. However, we are not directly concerned with these mappings. The most important is that common-sense knows about a (small) number of proto-mathematical concepts, such as collections, sequences and count-numbers (positive integers). We know also about geometric simplifications such as line, circle, square, cube, etc. These common sense notions might even be the real roots of our mathematics. However, these kind of semi-formal abstractions do not play a very central role…

Note that Qualified does not partition into Allowed and Disallowed. Firstly, things can be Allowed by one Norm and Disallowed by another one. Secondly, the logical complement of the thing allowed by a permission is qualified (as worse or equal than the thing allowed), but neither allowed nor disallowed.

Occurrence.description: A consequence of our clear separation of ontology from models of situations (occurrences), is well exemplified in the two ways we look at time and space. Things happen against the canvas of space and time. This 3D canvas moving in time (or whatever metaphor) allows us to index instances of objects and processes. Time and space provide positions in time and space for objects. Positions are in general modeled in some mereological framework. However, the objects and processes as classes have time and space properties in a different way. Space occupied by an object is its inherent property of size or extension. This property was for Descartes even the critical one that separated mental (not: abstract) objects from physical ones. Processes occupy (consume) time; they take some duration. This time resource is inversely related to the consumption of energy. This distinction between position and extension is also made in various other ontologies. If a superior court adopts a persuasive precedent, it may become binding in the jurisdiction.

In lkif-core, the physical world evolves around two main classes: physical objects and processes. Objects are pieces of matter, while matter is typed by substances. Objects have mass, extension, viz. form and aggregation state (which limits form). Objects are the specification of the notion that matter, and in particular solid objects, is what makes the physical world relatively stable and observable. We define (physical) situations in the first place by the arrangement of physical objects (entities).

Prohibition.description: Prohibition obliges/allows thing(s), to which therefore the predication Obliged applies, and disallows thing(s), to which therefore the predication Disallowed applies. The union of the thing(s) allowed and the thing(s) disallowed is qualified by the prohibition. The things allowed and disallowed by the prohibition are disjoint (and completely partition the space of things qualified). If S then O(A) means that S is qualified, S and A is obliged/allowed, and S and not A is disallowed. If S then F(A) means that S is qualified, S and A is disallowed, and S and not A is obliged/allowed. The difference between Obligation and Prohibition is in which part of the partition of the qualified space is explicitly described by the normative statement. Alternative label: directive. Equivalent to Obligation.

For LKIF the distinction between Belief, Intention, Qualification, and Observation is relevant. The distinction between belief/expectation, intention, and observation is relevant for i.a. establishing mens rea (guilty mind). The distinction between beliefs (expressing the content of the mind of an agent) and statements (expressing the content of an act of communication by an agent) is classical.

Statute_BEARS_Norm.description: A Medium 'bears' or carries expressions. LKIF also names the inverse, 'medium'. Every Statute has one or more 'bears' that is a Norm.

Agent_BELIEVES_Belief.description: Relates an agent to the belief(s) it holds. LKIF also names the inverse, 'believed by'. Every 'believed by' of a Belief is an Agent. Every Belief has one or more 'believed by' that is an Agent.

TemporalOccurrence_BETWEEN_PairOfPeriods.description: Specifies that a time period occurs between two other periods.

Qualification_COMMANDS_Obliged.description: LKIF also names the inverse, 'commanded by'.

PairOfPeriods_COMPONENT_TemporalOccurren.description: Specifies that some thing is a (functional) component of some other thing. LKIF also names the inverse, 'component of'. Every 'component' of a PairOfPeriods is a TemporalOccurrence.

Thing_COMPONENT_Thing.description: Specifies that some thing is a (functional) component of some other thing. LKIF also names the inverse, 'component of'.

Thing_COMPOSES_Thing.description: Specifies that some thing is composed_of (spatially) within some other thing. LKIF also names the inverse, 'composed of'. Transitive.

Place_CONNECT_Place.description: Two places are connected if they are both relatively fixed and when they meet.

Thing_CONTAINS_Thing.description: Specifies that some thing is contained (spatially) within some other thing. LKIF also names the inverse, 'contained in'. Transitive.

EpistemicRole_CONTEXT_MentalProcess.description: The context property relates a subjective entity to the context in which the entity holds. Every EpistemicRole has one or more 'context' that is a MentalProcess.

SubjectiveEntity_CONTEXT_Thing.description: The context property relates a subjective entity to the context in which the entity holds. Every SubjectiveEntity has one or more 'context' that is a Thing.

Thing_CONTEXT_Thing.description: The context property relates a subjective entity to the context in which the entity holds. Each Thing has at most one Thing.

Thing_COUNTS_AS_Thing.description: The counts-as relation of Searle (1995) is used to express the creation of observer-relative or social facts such as the playing of roles or having a function.

Place_COVER_Place.description: Definition cover: cover(a, b) iff forall x:( meet(x, b) implies meet(x, a) ). Specifies that two places cover eachother. Note: this cover-relation is the inverse of the COV relation described by Donnelly (2005). To add in OWL 1.1: 'cover' is reflexive, 'cover' is transitive. LKIF also names the inverse, 'covered by'. Transitive.

Change_CREATION_Thing.description: Specifies that some thing is created (i.e. a result of) by a process, and exists because of the process taking place. LKIF also names the inverse, 'created by'.

Creation_CREATION_Thing.description: Specifies that some thing is created (i.e. a result of) by a process, and exists because of the process taking place. LKIF also names the inverse, 'created by'. Every Creation has one or more 'creation' that is a Thing.

Decision_CREATION_Promise.description: Specifies that some thing is created (i.e. a result of) by a process, and exists because of the process taking place. LKIF also names the inverse, 'created by'. Every Decision has one or more 'creation' that is a Promise.

Decision_CREATION_StatementInWriting.description: Specifies that some thing is created (i.e. a result of) by a process, and exists because of the process taking place. LKIF also names the inverse, 'created by'. Every Decision has one or more 'creation' that is a StatementInWriting.

SpeechAct_CREATION_CommunicatedAttitude.description: Specifies that some thing is created (i.e. a result of) by a process, and exists because of the process taking place. LKIF also names the inverse, 'created by'. Every SpeechAct has one or more 'creation' that is a CommunicatedAttitude.

Declaration_DECLARES_Expression.description: Relates a declaration to the expression being declared. LKIF also names the inverse, 'declared by'. Every Declaration has one or more 'declares' that is an Expression.

Change_DIRECT_PART_Continuation.description: The non-transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'direct part of'. Every Continuation has one or more 'direct part of' that is a Change.

Change_DIRECT_PART_Initiation.description: The non-transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'direct part of'. Every Initiation has one or more 'direct part of' that is a Change.

Change_DIRECT_PART_Termination.description: The non-transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'direct part of'. Every Termination has one or more 'direct part of' that is a Change.

Thing_DIRECT_PART_Thing.description: The non-transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'direct part of'.

Transaction_DIRECT_PART_Action.description: The non-transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'direct part of'. Every 'direct part' of a Transaction is an Action. Every Transaction has exactly two 'direct part' that is an Action.

Prohibition_DISALLOWS_Disallowed.description: Relates a norm to the thing it disallows. LKIF also names the inverse, 'disallowed by'. Every 'disallows' of a Prohibition is a Disallowed. Every Prohibition has one or more 'disallows' that is a Disallowed. Every Disallowed has one or more 'disallowed by' that is a Prohibition.

Qualification_DISALLOWS_Disallowed.description: Relates a norm to the thing it disallows. LKIF also names the inverse, 'disallowed by'.

TemporalOccurrence_DURING_TemporalOccurr.description: Specifies that a time period occurs during another period.

EvaluativeAttitude_EVALUATES_EvaluativeP.description: LKIF also names the inverse, 'evaluated by'. Every 'evaluates' of an EvaluativeAttitude is an EvaluativeProposition. Every EvaluativeAttitude has one or more 'evaluates' that is an EvaluativeProposition. Every EvaluativeProposition has one or more 'evaluated by' that is an EvaluativeAttitude.

EvaluativeProposition_EVALUATIVELY_COMPA.description: Expresses whether some thing is evaluatively comparable to some other thing. Symmetric. Every EvaluativeProposition has one or more 'evaluatively comparable' that is an EvaluativeProposition. Every 'evaluatively comparable' of an EvaluativeProposition is an EvaluativeProposition.

Place_EXACTLY_COINCIDE_Place.description: Definition exactly-coincide: exactly-coincide(a, b) iff forall x:( meet(x, a) iff meet(x, b) ). To add in OWL 1.1: 'exactly-coincide' is reflexive, 'exactly-coincide' is symetric, 'exactly-coincide' is transitive. Symmetric. Transitive.

Place_EXTERNALLY_CONNECT_Place.description: Two places are externally connected if they are relatively fixed and abut, but do not overlap (OWL 1.1).

TemporalOccurrence_FINISHES_TemporalOccu.description: Specifies that a time period finishes another period, i.e. the other period starts before, but ends at the same moment.

Agent_HOLDS_MentalEntity.description: Relates an agent to the propositional attitude it holds. LKIF also names the inverse, 'held by'. Every 'holds' of an Agent is a MentalEntity.

Agent_HOLDS_MentalObject.description: Relates an agent to the propositional attitude it holds. LKIF also names the inverse, 'held by'. Every 'held by' of a MentalObject is an Agent. Every MentalObject has one or more 'held by' that is an Agent.

TemporalOccurrence_IMMEDIATELY_AFTER_Tem.description: 'is_met_by' is renamed to 'immediately_after'. Add to OWL 1.1: 'immediately_after' is serial, 'immediately_after' is irreflexive. Specifies that a time period occurs immediately after another period, i.e. it starts where the other period ends. LKIF also names the inverse, 'immediately before'. Every TemporalOccurrence has one or more 'immediately after' that is a TemporalOccurrence. Every TemporalOccurrence has one or more 'immediately before' that is a TemporalOccurrence.

SubjectiveEntity_IMPOSED_ON_Thing.description: Specifies that some subjective entity is imposed on some thing. Every SubjectiveEntity has one or more 'imposed on' that is a Thing.

Thing_IMPOSED_ON_Thing.description: Specifies that some subjective entity is imposed on some thing. Each Thing has at most one Thing.

Place_IN_Place.description: The 'in' property is used to express that one place is located (i.e. contained) within another place. It is therefore a mereological relation as well.

Agent_INTENDS_Intention.description: Specifies that the agent holds some intention. LKIF also names the inverse, 'intended by'. Every 'intended by' of an Intention is an Agent. Every Intention has one or more 'intended by' that is an Agent.

Place_LOCATION_COMPLEX_LocationComplex.description: LKIF also names the inverse, 'location complex for'. Every 'location complex for' of a LocationComplex is a Place. Every LocationComplex has one or more 'location complex for' that is a Place. Every Place has one or more 'location complex' that is a LocationComplex. Every 'location complex' of a Place is a LocationComplex.

Place_MEET_Place.description: Specifies that two places meet, but need not overlap or cover (reflexive). To add in OWL 1.1: 'meet' is equivalent with ('abut' union 'partially-coincide'). Symmetric.

Organisation_MEMBER_Organisation.description: Specifies membership of a set or group. LKIF also names the inverse, 'member of'. Every 'member' of an Organisation is one of Organisation, Person.

Organisation_MEMBER_Person.description: Specifies membership of a set or group. LKIF also names the inverse, 'member of'. Every 'member' of an Organisation is one of Organisation, Person. Every Organisation has one or more 'member' that is a Person.

Thing_MEMBER_Thing.description: Specifies membership of a set or group. LKIF also names the inverse, 'member of'.

NormativelyQualified_NORMATIVELY_COMPARA.description: Every NormativelyQualified has one or more 'normatively comparable' that is a NormativelyQualified.

NormativelyQualified_NORMATIVELY_EQUIVAL.description: LKIF also names the inverse, 'normatively equivalent or worse'. Transitive. Every Allowed has one or more 'normatively equivalent or worse' that is a NormativelyQualified.

Disallowed_NORMATIVELY_STRICTLY_BETTER_A.description: LKIF also names the inverse, 'normatively strictly worse'. Transitive. Every Disallowed has one or more 'normatively strictly better' that is an Allowed.

Disallowed_NORMATIVELY_STRICTLY_BETTER_O.description: LKIF also names the inverse, 'normatively strictly worse'. Transitive. Every Obliged has one or more 'normatively strictly worse' that is a Disallowed.

Agent_OBSERVES_Belief.description: Relates an agent to the thing it beliefs it observes. LKIF also names the inverse, 'observer'.

Place_OVERLAP_Place.description: Two places overlap if they are relatively fixed and partially coincide.

TemporalOccurrence_OVERLAP_TemporalOccur.description: Specifies that a time period overlaps with another time period (in any way).

Change_PART_Change.description: Transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'part of'. Transitive. Every 'part' of a Change is a Change.

Plan_PART_Action.description: Transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'part of'. Transitive. Every 'part' of a Plan is one of Action, Plan. Every Plan has one or more 'part' that is an Action.

Plan_PART_Plan.description: Transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'part of'. Transitive. Every 'part' of a Plan is one of Action, Plan.

Thing_PART_Thing.description: Transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'part of'. Transitive.

Place_PARTIALLY_COINCIDE_Place.description: Definition partially-coincide: partially-coincide(a, b) iff exists x :( cover(a, x) and cover(b, x) ). To add in OWL 1.1: 'partially-coincide' is reflexive, 'partially-coincide' is disjoint with 'abut'. Symmetric.

Change_PARTICIPANT_Agent.description: A participant is someone or something that participates in a change, i.e. is involved in a change. LKIF also names the inverse, 'participant in'. Every 'participant in' of an Agent is a Change.

Change_PARTICIPANT_Thing.description: A participant is someone or something that participates in a change, i.e. is involved in a change. LKIF also names the inverse, 'participant in'.

Agent_PLAYS_LegalRole.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every LegalRole has one or more 'played by' that is an Agent. Every 'played by' of a LegalRole is an Agent.

Agent_PLAYS_OrganisationRole.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every 'played by' of an OrganisationRole is an Agent.

Agent_PLAYS_Role.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every 'plays' of an Agent is a Role.

Agent_PLAYS_SocialRole.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every 'played by' of a SocialRole is an Agent. Every SocialRole has one or more 'played by' that is an Agent.

Artifact_PLAYS_Function.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every Artifact has one or more 'plays' that is a Function.

Disallowed_PLAYS_ObservationOfViolation.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every ObservationOfViolation has one or more 'played by' that is a Disallowed.

Expression_PLAYS_Argument.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every Argument has one or more 'played by' that is an Expression.

MentalObject_PLAYS_EpistemicRole.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every 'played by' of an EpistemicRole is a MentalObject. Every EpistemicRole has one or more 'played by' that is a MentalObject.

Person_PLAYS_PersonRole.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every PersonRole has one or more 'played by' that is a Person. Every 'played by' of a PersonRole is a Person.

Person_PLAYS_ProfessionalLegalRole.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every 'played by' of a ProfessionalLegalRole is a Person.

PhysicalObject_PLAYS_Function.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every Function has one or more 'played by' that is a PhysicalObject. Every 'played by' of a Function is a PhysicalObject.

Proposition_PLAYS_Assumption.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every Assumption has one or more 'played by' that is a Proposition.

Proposition_PLAYS_Evidence.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every Evidence has one or more 'played by' that is a Proposition.

Proposition_PLAYS_Exception.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every Exception has one or more 'played by' that is a Proposition.

Proposition_PLAYS_Expectation.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every Expectation has one or more 'played by' that is a Proposition.

Proposition_PLAYS_Fact.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every Fact has one or more 'played by' that is a Proposition.

Proposition_PLAYS_Reason.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every Reason has one or more 'played by' that is a Proposition.

Thing_PLAYS_Observation.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every Observation has one or more 'played by' that is a Thing.

Thing_PLAYS_Role.description: Specifies that some thing plays a role. LKIF also names the inverse, 'played by'. Every Role has one or more 'played by' that is a Thing.

TemporalOccurrence_PRECEEDS_TemporalOccu.description: Specifies that a time period preceeds another period, the periods do not overlap.

Promise_PROMISES_Expression.description: Relates a promise to the expression being promised. LKIF also names the inverse, 'promised by'. Every Promise has one or more 'promises' that is an Expression.

Norm_QUALIFIES_NormativelyQualified.description: Relates an evaluative attitude or qualification to the proposition or thing being qualified. LKIF also names the inverse, 'qualified by'. Every NormativelyQualified has one or more 'qualified by' that is a Norm. Every Norm has one or more 'qualifies' that is a NormativelyQualified.

Qualification_QUALIFIES_Qualified.description: Relates an evaluative attitude or qualification to the proposition or thing being qualified. LKIF also names the inverse, 'qualified by'. Every 'qualifies' of a Qualification is a Qualified. Every Qualification has one or more 'qualifies' that is a Qualified. Every Qualified has one or more 'qualified by' that is a Qualification.

Qualified_QUALITATIVELY_COMPARABLE_Quali.description: Symmetric. Every Qualified has one or more 'qualitatively comparable' that is a Qualified. Every 'qualitatively comparable' of a Qualified is a Qualified.

Place_RELATIVELY_FIXED_Place.description: NOTE: This cannot currently be expressed using OWL DL. Two places are relatively fixed if and only if either x and y have a common reference object or neither x nor y has a reference object. Symmetric. Transitive.

Change_REQUIREMENT_Thing.description: A requirement relation relates the process with a prerequisite for that process: without it the process cannot occur. LKIF also names the inverse, 'requirement of'. Every Change has one or more 'requirement' that is a Thing.

Continuation_REQUIREMENT_Initiation.description: A requirement relation relates the process with a prerequisite for that process: without it the process cannot occur. LKIF also names the inverse, 'requirement of'. Every Continuation has one or more 'requirement' that is an Initiation.

Termination_REQUIREMENT_Continuation.description: A requirement relation relates the process with a prerequisite for that process: without it the process cannot occur. LKIF also names the inverse, 'requirement of'. Every Termination has one or more 'requirement' that is a Continuation.

Change_RESOURCE_Thing.description: A resource is some quantity of something used to perform the action: i.e. time, energy. LKIF also names the inverse, 'resource for'.

Process_RESOURCE_TemporalOccurrence.description: A resource is some quantity of something used to perform the action: i.e. time, energy. LKIF also names the inverse, 'resource for'. Every Process has one or more 'resource' that is a TemporalOccurrence.

Change_RESULT_Thing.description: Specifies that some participant is the result of the process, it might have existed before the process took place, but is in some way altered. LKIF also names the inverse, 'result of'. Every Change has one or more 'result' that is a Thing.

Creation_RESULT_Artifact.description: Specifies that some participant is the result of the process, it might have existed before the process took place, but is in some way altered. LKIF also names the inverse, 'result of'. Every Artifact has one or more 'result of' that is a Creation.

Initiation_RESULT_Continuation.description: Specifies that some participant is the result of the process, it might have existed before the process took place, but is in some way altered. LKIF also names the inverse, 'result of'. Every Initiation has one or more 'result' that is a Continuation.

Place_SPATIAL_REFERENCE_Thing.description: The reference to an object determines the relative place.

RelativePlace_SPATIAL_REFERENCE_Thing.description: The reference to an object determines the relative place. Every RelativePlace has one or more 'spatial reference' that is a Thing.

Place_SPATIAL_RELATION_Place.description: A spatial relation is a relation between two places.

TemporalOccurrence_STARTS_TemporalOccurr.description: Specifies that a time period starts another period, i.e. the other period starts at the same time, but ends at a later time.

CommunicatedAttitude_STATES_Expression.description: Relates an author to its statements. LKIF also names the inverse, 'stated by'. Every 'states' of a CommunicatedAttitude is an Expression. Every CommunicatedAttitude has one or more 'states' that is an Expression. Every 'stated by' of an Expression is a CommunicatedAttitude. Every Expression has one or more 'stated by' that is a CommunicatedAttitude.

CommunicatedAttitude_STATES_Proposition.description: Relates an author to its statements. LKIF also names the inverse, 'stated by'.

StatementInWriting_STATES_Expression.description: Relates an author to its statements. LKIF also names the inverse, 'stated by'. Every StatementInWriting has one or more 'states' that is an Expression.

Composition_STRICT_PART_Part.description: Non transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'strict part of'. Every Composition has two or more 'strict part' that is a Part.

Pair_STRICT_PART_Part.description: Non transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'strict part of'. Every Pair has exactly two 'strict part' that is a Part.

Thing_STRICT_PART_Thing.description: Non transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'strict part of'.

Transaction_STRICT_PART_Assignment.description: Non transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'strict part of'. Every Assignment has one or more 'strict part of' that is a Transaction.

Transaction_STRICT_PART_Delegation.description: Non transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'strict part of'. Every Delegation has one or more 'strict part of' that is a Transaction.

Transaction_STRICT_PART_Mandate.description: Non transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'strict part of'. Every Mandate has one or more 'strict part of' that is a Transaction.

Whole_STRICT_PART_Part.description: Non transitive part relation. LKIF also names the inverse, 'strict part of'. Every 'strict part of' of a Part is a Whole. Every Part has one or more 'strict part of' that is a Whole. Every 'strict part' of a Whole is a Part. Every Whole has one or more 'strict part' that is a Part.

TemporalOccurrence_TEMPORAL_RELATION_Tem.description: A relation between two time periods.

BeliefInViolation_TOWARDS_Disallowed.description: A towards relation between a propositional attitude and a proposition expresses that the attitude is held towards that proposition. Qualification of the proposition can be either true or false, i.e. the attitude denotes whether the proposition is either true or false. LKIF also names the inverse, 'attitude'. Every BeliefInViolation has one or more 'towards' that is a Disallowed.

DisallowedIntention_TOWARDS_Disallowed.description: A towards relation between a propositional attitude and a proposition expresses that the attitude is held towards that proposition. Qualification of the proposition can be either true or false, i.e. the attitude denotes whether the proposition is either true or false. LKIF also names the inverse, 'attitude'. Every DisallowedIntention has one or more 'towards' that is a Disallowed.

PropositionalAttitude_TOWARDS_LegalExpre.description: A towards relation between a propositional attitude and a proposition expresses that the attitude is held towards that proposition. Qualification of the proposition can be either true or false, i.e. the attitude denotes whether the proposition is either true or false. LKIF also names the inverse, 'attitude'. Every LegalExpression has one or more 'attitude' that is a PropositionalAttitude.

PropositionalAttitude_TOWARDS_Propositio.description: A towards relation between a propositional attitude and a proposition expresses that the attitude is held towards that proposition. Qualification of the proposition can be either true or false, i.e. the attitude denotes whether the proposition is either true or false. LKIF also names the inverse, 'attitude'. Every 'towards' of a PropositionalAttitude is a Proposition. Every PropositionalAttitude has one or more 'towards' that is a Proposition. Every 'attitude' of a Proposition is a PropositionalAttitude.

Agent_UTTERS_CommunicatedAttitude.description: Relates an agent to its utterance(s). LKIF also names the inverse, 'utterer'. Every CommunicatedAttitude has one or more 'utterer' that is an Agent.
